decisions.notes: The noun phrase means time between arriving and departing connecting services. BA directly uses connection times. The short-connection example and Chinese agree without guaranteeing that any particular interval is sufficient.

BA defines this as the limit by which check-in must be completed. The revised actual-use sentence now demonstrates finishing before that deadline, with exact Chinese alignment; it is distinct from boarding time.
The verb phrase concerns failure to catch an onward service. The conditional flight-delay example and scoped Chinese aliases are accurate, with genuine complete-phrase inflections.
Osaka Metro directly calls the button used to signal getting off a stop button. The bus/library example and Chinese fit that scoped usage, not an emergency-stop mechanism.

Stagecoach directly describes bus services being suspended for a period. The row scopes suspension to temporary lack of service, not merely a closed stop. POS and Chinese match the travel consequence in the example.
University of Iowa describes documenting existing unit condition on a move-in checklist. Recording the cracked window is a useful original example, distinct from a packing list.
Braintree Council directly uses this phrase for transferring a facility. The landlord/tenant scenario and separable-verb meaning are natural; handing keys over is not making duplicate keys.
Bury Council directly uses lease expiry dates. The phrase, expiry-date calendar example and Chinese are precise without assuming any jurisdictional consequence of expiry.
Fife Council directly distinguishes renewing an existing lease. The revised tenants asking to renew their lease for another year is natural and accurately translated.
This is an amount removed from a previously paid deposit. The missing-key statement is a plausible fictional example; the definition does not claim any deduction is automatically justified.
Berkeley Housing directly uses maintenance request for resident repair issues. The broken-heater scenario and Chinese repair-request noun match the service.
Westminster distinguishes urgent danger/structural problems. A burst-pipe repair is a suitable original use, with no unsupported universal service deadline or repair instructions.
Fife explains moist air condensing into water on a cold surface, including windows. The droplet example is accurate and does not confuse condensation with a building leak.

Renfrewshire explicitly discusses water leaking from ceilings and different possible origins. The damp-patch sentence, noun meaning and aliases agree without falsely naming the roof as the necessary cause.
ASSA ABLOY primary terminology and product material support the key-operated lock component. Replacing the damaged cylinder is accurately translated as replacing the core, not the whole lock.
Spare here means kept as an extra for use when needed. Giving a sister an extra key is natural original usage and the Chinese aliases identify the same object.

NHS describes the tummy feeling full/uncomfortable. The selected verb phrase and Chinese symptom wording match, avoiding the malformed or unrelated source senses of bloating. No cause or treatment is inferred.
NHS defines acid travelling upward from the stomach. The nurse-symptom example is natural, and the row distinguishes the condition/description from diagnosing every burning or sour sensation.
MedlinePlus uses stuffy nose as a symptom. Nasal blockage and difficulty smelling the soup are semantically aligned; the row does not equate every case with a cold.
NHS authenticates the condition and eye discomfort. The plural head, dry-eye/video-call example and Chinese are consistent; no singular form is borrowed from an unrelated head.
NHS distinguishes ligament sprains from muscle strains. The ankle-injury noun phrase and missed-walk example fit the scoped meaning and do not call it a fracture.

decisions.term: tingling in the hands and feet
decisions.notes: NHS discusses pricking/tingling in hands and feet. The aliases are specifically 刺麻/针刺感, not all complete numbness, and the example only reports a sensation.
Cambridge explicitly defines being more readily affected by cold. The flatmate comparison and extra-clothing context naturally express sensitivity, not psychological fear.
NHS treats this as internal mouth dryness. Difficulty speaking through a presentation is a plausible original use, and the row excludes the different cracked-lips condition.
NHLBI defines insufficient sleep and notes possible attention effects. The lecture example is natural and does not turn ordinary short sleep into a necessary insomnia diagnosis.
Microsoft directly documents unlocking accounts. The selected action restores use of a locked account; failed-sign-in context and Chinese are accurate without claiming new account registration.

After revision, the definition broadly checks a claimed identity and treats documents/evidence as possible methods, not a necessary paper-document step. This matches NIST scope; the account activation example is natural.
USPS directly uses the phrase for updating addresses. The ordinary office-notification example and plural changes of address are correct and do not equate every update with mail forwarding.
The noun denotes information confirming appointment arrangements. An email containing a clinic address is a useful original context, with no implication of rescheduling.
National Rail distinguishes changing an existing ticket from cancellation/refund. The tomorrow-train example and Chinese travel aliases fit the verb phrase; no universal exchange right is promised.
The row selects application materials not yet supplied. A clerk sending a list is a natural context; singular missing document is a genuine number variant, not an unrelated canonical head.

After revision, electronic marks/data express signing or authenticating a document, not merely displaying identity. This respects the Law Commission distinction; the form example is accurately translated and makes no universal validity claim.
Cambridge authenticates an official permission document for residence. Checking its expiry before travel is natural and the Chinese correctly distinguishes it from proof of address.

aliasDecisions.notes: Both Chinese aliases denote the baggage-retrieval area already defined by this exact US travel noun phrase. No new lost-property sense is introduced.
机舱行李 denotes the existing cabin/carry-on luggage sense, not checked baggage; the original body and example remain exact.
嗓子哑 is a concise colloquial equivalent of the existing hoarse-voice adjective, and the entry already covers 嗓子哑了.
延期申请 refers to the same request for a later deadline as existing 申请延期. The exact body still states that asking does not mean approval.

scope: Actual 33 final EN/ZH/POS/Chinese aliases/forms rows and all four original alias target bodies read. Lexical meanings only; no medical treatment, dosing, legal entitlement or current transport schedule is taught. Primary dictionaries, health bodies, institutions, manufacturers and service providers were consulted; inaccessible Cambridge direct pages were not represented as successful fetches, and publisher-indexed text was used where available.
resolvedRevisions: identity verification no longer requires submitted identity documents in every case.
electronic signature now requires signing/authenticating-document intent, not an identity marker alone.
check-in deadline now has a meaningful completed-before-deadline example.
renew a lease now has a natural their lease tenant example.
